knowledge:
- key_parameters: model_type=Specifies the mixture model type in mixtureModel(), which can be "linear" (default), "spline", "polynomial", or "one_dimensional" ;; posterior_cutoff=The posterior probability threshold (default 0.75) above which a cell is considered compromised and removed ;; keep_all_below_boundary=Boolean (default TRUE) in plotFiltering() and filterCells() that keeps all cells below the intact cell line, preventing low-mitochondrial cells from being incorrectly excluded ;; enforce_left_cutoff=Boolean (default TRUE) in plotFiltering() and filterCells() that prevents a U-shaped boundary by discarding all cells with both lower complexity and higher mitochondrial percentage than the lowest-mito cell marked for removal
- alternatives: Standard arbitrary mitochondrial percentage thresholds, or identifying outliers using median absolute deviation (MAD) (recommended when the two-distribution assumption is not met)
- when_to_use: When performing quality control on single-cell RNA-seq datasets (especially from tissues like archived tumors where standard arbitrary mitochondrial thresholds are too stringent) and there is a non-trivial number of compromised cells, characterized by a triangular shape in a plot of mitochondrial percentage vs. detected genes
- pitfalls: Running miQC on datasets without a significant number of compromised cells (where the two-distribution assumption is violated), which causes mixtureModel() to throw a warning and fail to filter cells ;; excluding low-mitochondrial cells near the x-intercept of the compromised line (resolved by setting keep_all_below_boundary = TRUE) ;; U-shaped decision boundaries keeping worse cells while discarding better ones (resolved by setting enforce_left_cutoff = TRUE)

workflows.name: standard_2d_miqc
workflows.intent: Perform quality control filtering on single-cell RNA-seq data by jointly modeling mitochondrial read percentage and the number of detected genes using a 2D mixture model.
input: sce (a SingleCellExperiment object containing raw count data)
workflows.stages: 1. Identify mitochondrial genes and calculate per-cell QC metrics using scater::addPerCellQC ;; 2. Plot QC metrics to visually inspect the dataset using plotMetrics ;; 3. Fit a 2D mixture model (linear, spline, or polynomial) using mixtureModel ;; 4. Inspect model parameters and posterior probabilities using parameters and posterior ;; 5. Visualize the fitted model and filtering boundary using plotModel and plotFiltering ;; 6. Filter out compromised cells from the SingleCellExperiment object using filterCells
workflows.code:
mt_genes <- grepl("^mt-",  rownames(sce))
feature_ctrls <- list(mito = rownames(sce)[mt_genes])
sce <- addPerCellQC(sce, subsets = feature_ctrls)
plotMetrics(sce)
model <- mixtureModel(sce)
parameters(model)
head(posterior(model))
plotModel(sce, model)
plotFiltering(sce, model)
sce <- filterCells(sce, model)

# Alternative non-linear models
model2 <- mixtureModel(sce, model_type = "spline")
plotModel(sce, model2)
plotFiltering(sce, model2)

model3 <- mixtureModel(sce, model_type = "polynomial")
plotModel(sce, model3)
plotFiltering(sce, model3)

# Adjusting filtering parameters for cancer datasets
plotFiltering(sce, model, posterior_cutoff = 0.6, enforce_left_cutoff = TRUE, keep_all_below_boundary = TRUE)

workflows.name: one_dimensional_miqc
workflows.intent: Perform quality control filtering based solely on mitochondrial percentage using a 1D Gaussian mixture model to calculate a single threshold.
input: sce (a SingleCellExperiment object containing raw count data)
workflows.stages: 1. Identify mitochondrial genes and calculate per-cell QC metrics using scater::addPerCellQC ;; 2. Fit a 1D mixture model using mixtureModel with model_type = "one_dimensional" ;; 3. Visualize the model and filtering using plotModel and plotFiltering ;; 4. Calculate the single mitochondrial percentage cutoff using get1DCutoff
workflows.code:
mt_genes <- grepl("^mt-",  rownames(sce))
feature_ctrls <- list(mito = rownames(sce)[mt_genes])
sce <- addPerCellQC(sce, subsets = feature_ctrls)
model4 <- mixtureModel(sce, model_type = "one_dimensional")
plotModel(sce, model4)
plotFiltering(sce, model4)
get1DCutoff(sce, model4)
